gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's 350 W panel has a 33 V open-circuit voltage. Two in series reach 66 V, over the Elite 200 V2's 12–60 V solar input, and two in parallel are held to the station's 20 A limit, which caps them below 660 W (20 A × 33 V). So the $2,148 Elite 200 V2 + 2×350 W bundle cannot put 700 W into the station. Two SP200L 200 W panels (24.6 V Voc each, 49.2 V in series) do fit under the 60 V limit.
standout_why: I compared four pages. The Anker SOLIX cabin setup guide (cited) gives no Voc, current, connector or series/parallel limits and tells readers to 'confirm panel voltage, current, and connector compatibility' themselves. Its only input figure is the F3800's 2,400 W maximum. SolutionEnergy's cabin page (cited) has no voltage, current or wiring figures at all. The live search top results are Anker and BLUETTI blogs with sizing rules of thumb only. ChatGPT's own answer says only 'make sure the solar panels' voltage, current, and wiring configuration match.' None of these pages pairs a specific panel with a specific station input window.
decides: This confirms the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W SP200L kit ($1,499 on 2026-11-13) as the 400 W pick, wired in series: 49.2 V Voc is under the 60 V ceiling. In parallel the two panels' 21.6 A short-circuit current is over the 20 A input limit. It argues against stepping up to the 2×350 W bundle ($2,148). Series wiring is ruled out by the 60 V limit, and in parallel the 20 A limit keeps the input under 660 W. So the extra $649 buys less than its 700 W nameplate. Separately, the single 350 W kit price on BLUETTI's store is now $1,449, not the $1,249 on our page.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage, connector, listed compatibility
findings.value: Voc 33 V; MC4 with a 20 A MC4-to-XT60 cable, 1.5 m, included; Elite 200 V2 and AC180 are on its compatible list; $649
findings.note: The page does not list Isc, Vmp or Imp. Its IP rating conflicts: IP67 in the features section, IP65 in the FAQ.

findings.label: Series/parallel limit (derived)
findings.value: Series: 2 × 33 V = 66 V Voc, over the 60 V input maximum. Parallel: capped at 20 A, so under 20 A × 33 V = 660 W, short of the 700 W nameplate
findings.note: Arithmetic from the 33 V Voc (panel page) and the 12–60 V/20 A input (Elite 200 V2 page). 660 W is a ceiling: real Vmp is below Voc, so actual input is lower. BLUETTI does not publish this pairing limit. Bundle price $2,148 from storecheck: https://www.bluettipower.com/products/elite-200-v2-2-pv350d

findings.label: Electrical specs and compatibility
findings.value: Voc 24.6 V, Isc 10.8 A, MC4; Elite 200 V2 and AC180 on its compatible list; $399 single
findings.note: BLUETTI says mixing different panel types 'is not encouraged'. The page has no series/parallel instructions.

findings.label: Correct wiring for the 2×200 W kit (derived)
findings.value: Series: 49.2 V Voc, inside 12–60 V, at 10.8 A. Parallel: 21.6 A Isc, over the 20 A input limit
findings.note: 2 × 24.6 V = 49.2 V; 2 × 10.8 A = 21.6 A. Checked against the 12–60 V/20 A input on the Elite 200 V2 page. The station should cap current rather than be damaged, but series wiring stays inside both limits.
